=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Executive view

The Seller’s package is materially seller-favourable. The “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and “no further scrutiny” labels have no contractual effect and should not constrain the Buyer’s review. Several disclosed matters are potentially inconsistent with the agreed **debt-free/cash-free, 100% acquisition** and should be addressed as completion conditions, price adjustments, specific indemnities or express warranty protections.

## Material issues and pushback

### 1. Bluefen consent and customer concentration — **critical**

Bluefen represents approximately **30% of FY26 revenue** and its contract contains change-control provisions. No final consent or evidence that conditions have been satisfied has been provided.

**Push back:**

- Make delivery of an unconditional written Bluefen consent, and satisfaction of all related conditions, a **condition precedent to Completion**.
- Include a long-stop date and Buyer termination right.
- If consent is not obtained, give the Buyer a right to walk away or require a substantial price adjustment.
- Obtain confirmation that Bluefen will not terminate, reduce scope, reprice or otherwise adversely amend the relationship.
- Require an indemnity for losses arising from failure to obtain consent or any pre-Completion breach.

“Reasonable endeavours” is inadequate for a customer representing 30% of revenue.

### 2. Riverlark debt and security — **critical**

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding**, and the Seller proposes a release only after Completion. That is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free transaction and exposes the Buyer to enforcement and security risks.

**Push back:**

- Require repayment of the facility and release/discharge of all security **at or before Completion**, with evidence delivered at Completion.
- Pay the lender directly from the Completion funds if necessary.
- Include the debt, accrued interest, break costs and release costs in the completion accounts or purchase-price adjustment.
- Obtain appropriate PPSR and corporate-register searches and releases.
- Do not accept a post-Completion release as sufficient protection.

### 3. Completion bonuses and omitted AUD 420,000 liability — **critical**

The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, are not included in the funds flow, and may attract payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.

**Push back:**

- Require the Seller to bear all bonuses and associated payroll tax, superannuation, withholding and on-costs attributable to pre-Completion arrangements.
- Include the gross amount in the Completion funds flow or deduct it from the purchase price.
- Obtain a specific indemnity for any related liability.
- Require confirmation that no additional transaction, retention or change-of-control bonuses exist.
- Prevent the Seller from using the Buyer’s post-Completion funds to satisfy Seller-created liabilities.

### 4. DD-006 export/privacy incident — **critical**

The incident potentially involves 1,240 records and the investigation is incomplete. The Seller’s characterisation as “preliminary” does not remove the risk of privacy complaints, regulatory notification, remediation costs or affected-customer claims.

**Push back:**

- Require a full incident report before Completion, including access logs, recipients, scope, containment and notification analysis.
- Require compliance with the Privacy Act and any applicable Notifiable Data Breaches obligations.
- Obtain representations regarding containment, notices and regulator/customer communications.
- Add a specific indemnity covering investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory penalties to the extent insurable/lawfully recoverable, claims and legal costs.
- Require the Seller to control or appropriately coordinate pre-Completion remediation, with Buyer consent for material communications.

This should not be left under the general warranty regime.

### 5. Ironquay IP and SOW3 materials

The relevant contract apparently requires payment of every SOW3 fee before transfer of the Project Materials. AUD 180,000 remains open and there is no evidence of payment or assignment.

The Seller’s existing indemnity appears too narrow if it only covers a particular payment.

**Push back:**

- Require payment and assignment/transfer of all required IP before Completion, or retain the amount from the purchase price in escrow.
- Obtain executed assignment documents and evidence of chain of title.
- Expand the indemnity to cover all losses arising from failure to obtain the materials, third-party claims, replacement development and infringement/non-use risk.
- Require broader IP warranties covering ownership, employee/contractor assignments, open-source compliance, third-party infringement and freedom to use.

### 6. General disclosure and data-room disclosure

The blanket disclosure of the entire data room and public registers is unacceptable as a substitute for proper disclosure. It risks neutralising the warranty package by treating every document as disclosure regardless of relevance or prominence.

**Push back:**

- Require disclosures to be **specific, fair, accurate and reasonably apparent**, with document references and sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the risk.
- Exclude generic data-room and public-register disclosure from qualifying warranties.
- Confirm that disclosed matters do not waive claims for fraud, deliberate concealment, breach of fundamental warranties or specific indemnities.
- Require an updated disclosure letter immediately before Completion.

### 7. Buyer knowledge and non-reliance

The proposed knowledge exclusion is overly broad. It includes anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, and anything discoverable from the data room or public records. That creates constructive knowledge and may penalise ordinary due diligence.

**Push back:**

- Limit the exclusion to the **actual knowledge** of specifically named Buyer representatives.
- Do not impute knowledge from external advisers unless expressly agreed.
- Do not treat mere availability or discoverability in the data room as knowledge.
- Preserve claims based on fraud, wilful concealment, misleading disclosure and breach of specific indemnities.
- Delete or tightly limit all-purpose non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording.

### 8. Liability caps, thresholds and time limits

The proposed general cap is **AUD 4.8 million**, with a AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket. These are not automatically acceptable merely because the Seller calls them market terms.

**Push back:**

- Fundamental/title/capacity warranties should be uncapped or subject to a substantially higher cap, with a longer survival period.
- Tax, IP, fraud, deliberate concealment, confidentiality, employee liabilities, debt, leakage and specific indemnities should be outside the general cap.
- The basket should not apply to fundamental matters, tax, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Claims should survive for at least the applicable statutory limitation period for tax, title and IP matters.
- Ensure notification requirements do not require a detailed quantified claim before the Buyer can reasonably assess loss.
- The cap should not apply to amounts recoverable under insurance, third-party recoveries or specific indemnities.

### 9. Supplier renewals — AUD 330,000

Three related supplier renewals are disclosed, but the letter does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course commitments.

**Push back:**

- Obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, related-party details and pricing.
- Require confirmation that no renewal was entered into outside the ordinary course or without Buyer consent.
- Treat unavoidable post-Completion commitments as a price adjustment or require Seller reimbursement.
- Add a warranty that there are no undisclosed renewal, minimum-spend or termination-payment obligations.

### 10. Office lease and Mossvale assignment restrictions

The disclosure does not establish whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required. The Seller’s description should not be accepted as a legal conclusion.

**Push back:**

- Review the actual change-of-control and assignment language.
- Obtain written waivers or consents where required before Completion.
- Make any required consent a condition precedent.
- Include indemnities for termination, acceleration, loss of rights or increased cost caused by the transaction.

### 11. Title to shares

A share register is evidence, but it is not a complete title package. It does not alone address liens, options, trusts, encumbrances, competing claims or the Seller’s power to transfer.

**Push back:**

Require warranties and deliverables confirming:

- Seller owns the shares beneficially and legally;
- shares are fully paid and free of all encumbrances;
- no options, pre-emption rights, trusts or competing claims exist;
- the register and ASIC records are accurate;
- valid executed transfers and original certificates are delivered;
- Buyer receives 100% of the issued shares and all associated rights.

### 12. Tax and IP should not be left to “general warranties”

The Seller’s assertion that tax and IP are “settled” is not enough. These are often long-tail and high-severity risks.

**Push back:**

- Include a standalone tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax liabilities, including payroll tax, superannuation, GST, unpaid withholding and transaction-related employment liabilities.
- Require IP-specific warranties and indemnities.
- Exclude tax and IP claims from the general cap and short limitation period, or apply tailored caps and periods.

## Recommended negotiation position

Prioritise the following as non-negotiable:

1. **No Completion without Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment/security release.**
2. **Price adjustment or Seller-funded treatment of the AUD 420,000 bonuses and all on-costs.**
3. **Specific indemnities for the privacy incident, Ironquay IP, tax, debt/security and undisclosed employee liabilities.**
4. **Removal of blanket data-room disclosure and constructive Buyer-knowledge exclusions.**
5. **Separate, higher or uncapped protection for title, capacity, tax, IP, fraud and specific indemnities.**
6. **Completion deliverables for title, IP assignments, lender releases and required third-party consents.**
7. **Updated disclosure immediately before Completion and a robust no-leakage/no-new-commitments covenant.**

The Buyer should not accept the Seller’s “final” or “standard” labels as foreclosing these points. The disclosed facts themselves justify reopening the limitation and completion-risk allocation.
